lines: Appearance of several small skin lesions over the past two weeks
The patient, who was evaluated in the Obstetrics & Gynecology clinic approximately three months prior for genital lesions, now presents with new skin findings.
She recalls first noticing a single papule on her inner thigh about 14 days ago, which she initially ignored.
Since then, a few more have developed in nearby areas.
She denies pain, pruritus, or drainage from the lesions.
She has no history of similar skin problems and no systemic symptoms.
She did have one day of diarrhea about three weeks ago, which resolved spontaneously.

encounters.cc: Three days of worsening joint pain and fever

lines: Three days of worsening joint pain and fever

The patient is a 26-year-old female with a history of recurrent condylomata acuminata and prior molluscum contagiosum who presents to the emergency department with three days of worsening joint pain and fever.
She describes pain and swelling in her right knee, left wrist, and several fingers, along with difficulty gripping objects and walking.
She also reports a new, painful rash that started yesterday, consisting of red bumps and small blisters on her forearms and ankles.
For the past week, she has had intermittent lower abdominal discomfort and vaginal spotting.
She also mentions a yellowish vaginal discharge but denies itching or foul odor.
Her last menstrual period was two weeks ago.

She is sexually active with multiple partners, inconsistently using barrier protection.
She denies any history of IV drug use.
On exam, she is febrile and appears uncomfortable.
There is swelling and decreased range of motion in the left wrist and right knee, along with tenderness along the flexor tendons of her left hand.
Several pustular lesions with erythematous bases are seen on her distal extremities.
A speculum exam reveals a friable cervix with mucopurulent discharge.
No cervical motion tenderness is noted.
Blood cultures and synovial fluid analysis are obtained.
Nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) from cervical swab is positive.

She uses condoms inconsistently and is not on any form of contraception.
On physical examination, her temperature is 37.0°C, pulse is 80/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg.
Pelvic examination reveals the lesions shown in the image below, particularly in the labia minora and majora.
The lesions are exquisitely tender to touch.
There is bilateral tender, firm inguinal lymphadenopathy.
Painful genital ulcers and dysuria

The patient is a 28-year-old female with a history of condylomata acuminata, disseminated gonococcal infection, and primary genital herpes diagnosed in January 2025, who returns to the student health clinic and presents with 4 days of painful genital ulcers and dysuria.
She reports the discomfort began as burning and tingling in the genital area, followed by the development of small fluid-filled blisters that ruptured into shallow, tender ulcers.
She also reports low-grade fever, fatigue, and tender inguinal lymph nodes.
This is her first episode of genital symptoms.
